messages:
Maya (oncall): taking over night shift — quick summary of what I'm inheriting so we don't lose rhythm. active alerts: regen-service 5xx spike (p99 regen latency up, some customers seeing failures), embeddings-queue backpressure on eu-west1, and a noisy errorburst on tokenstore that started ~10m ago. primary=maya (me), secondary=ajit. timebox today = 4h until next handover.
Ajit: thanks — I'm shadowing for first 30m then can take primary at midnight if you need to step out. noted embedding queue + regen.
incident-bot: ALERT -> regen-service error-rate > 5% over 2m. Pager sent to eng-oncall. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-regen-4345
Maya (oncall): current mitigations in flight: 1) rate-shed non-critical regen routes (docs: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/regen-rate-shed) 2) fallback model variant warmstart (v2-small) on eu-west as fallback 3) increased retry window on client-proxy for 10s -> 30s to avoid thundering herd.
Sree: what's the fallback v2-small expected perf? will it increase latency?
Maya (oncall): v2-small is cpu cheaper, p95 latency ~120ms more but error-free for regen paths. customers with strict latency might see slower responses, but it avoids 500s. we've pre-warmed 4 replicas.
Noah: embedding queue backpressure — saw a spike in inflight messages on worker-3 (eu-west1). I've drained one hot shard and bumped consumer concurrency from 8 -> 12. Observability:
```
metric: embeddings_queue_inflight[eu-west1] = 124 -> 68 after drain
consumer_concurrency: 8 -> 12
```
Maya (oncall): nice. keep an eye on KV eviction rate — last night similar pattern caused regen faults when tokenstore hit mempressure.
Ajit: tokenstore mempressure — current free memory on auth-ks nodes: 14% on node-a, 22% on node-b. Ops-bot started an auto-evict earlier. I'm running a targeted cache trim on node-a now.
ops-bot: ACTION -> triggered cache-trim on auth-ks-node-a: `cache.trim --ratio 0.25` (initiated by Ajit).
Maya (oncall): customer impact: three customers (CUST-omega, CUST-lumen, CUST-rally) reported 500s for regen during a 5m window. Support has notified them and queued incident updates. No widespread data loss.
Sree: any rollout or recent model changes?
Maya (oncall): no model rollouts in the last 6h. We did push a config tweak to autoscaler for regen replicas but that was read-only. suspect cascade from tokenstore eviction + embedding backlog.
Ajit: I can take the fallback routing to 60% traffic to v2-small if the error-rate doesn't drop in 10m.
Maya (oncall): go for it if p10 error-rate >3% in 10m. I'll update the status page and add a note to the incident link.
Noah: logging note: regen-service is emitting duplicate span IDs for failed traces — opened a quick PR to de-dupe (link: https://git.redwood.ai/p/regen/patches/dupe-span). If that matches the timing, it's likely downstream parser choking and producing 500s.
Maya (oncall): good catch. For next steps: 1) Ajit to ramp fallback to v2-small at 60% after the 10m watch if errors persist. 2) Noah to continue with consumer concurrency observations and confirm embedding queue stays < 80. 3) Sree to monitor tokenstore free memory and pause any heavy background jobs. 4) Maya will keep status updates and coordinate comms with support.
Ajit: starting watch window now (10m). I'll post when I ramp.
Maya (oncall): running checklist snippet in case primary needs to hand off quickly:
```
- primary/secondary noted in thread
- active alerts + links
- running mitigations and who owns them
- customer list + support contact status
- next expected handover time
```
Maya (oncall): coverage gap note — between 01:15–01:45 UTC there's a planned oncall rotation overlap reduced by one (vacation cover). Ajit, can you extend to 01:50 if needed?
Ajit: yep ok to extend to 01:50.
incident-bot: UPDATE -> regen-service error-rate dropped to 1.8% over last 2m.
Maya (oncall): good sign. keep the watch. If error-rate goes back above 3% re-open ramp plan. Also posted a short blameless note to the incident page summarizing tokenstore mempressure link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-regen-4345/notes.
Sree: I'll pause the nightly batch job that writes to auth-ks at 01:00 UTC to remove extra pressure.
Maya (oncall): thanks — document that in the runbook step 4 (I updated it). I'll do final handover summary before I step out at 01:30 UTC. primary remains Maya until I explicitly pass to Ajit.
Noah: thumbs up. ping me if you want me to scale embedding workers back down after stabilise.
Maya (oncall): closing note for current state: alerts reduced, mitigation active (fallback warmed, consumer concurrency increased, cache-trim running), next check in 10m. I'll update last_message_ts when handing over. :white_check_mark:
